lxc_c559838c791ec4bf.text: What do kids in the USA eat for breakfast?

lxc_8d87a283c02021a9.text: How do they go to school?

lxc_daf3d7e2c0582a5b.text: Many kids ride a big yellow bus.

lxc_c8b80af7a5186c37.text: At school, they read, write, play and eat lunch with friends.

lxc_87b291940b5628c2.text: After school, they play and do homework.

lxc_37f2fa0fc83ec14d.text: You can follow one example day from morning to night.

lxc_21c9e25985f7185a.text: You can compare it with your day too.

lxc_3c14393d80340e89.text: It is seven o'clock in the morning.

lxc_cc27a3a5f5a7f4f3.text: Many children wake up at home.

lxc_5fdedf0234aee448.text: They get out of bed and wash their face.

lxc_67a78795ef1bd623.text: Then it is time for breakfast.

lxc_d2ee418a5141baf4.text: Many children eat cereal with milk.

lxc_186c77caccb99297.text: Cereal is small, dry pieces of grain in a bowl.

lxc_bb206dcd84e2ee6d.text: Some children eat eggs and toast.

lxc_677c78432bad923b.text: Some children eat fruit, like a banana or an apple.

lxc_8383ce778b824adf.text: Some children drink orange juice or milk.

lxc_7a09a6c48670b9d3.text: Some children eat breakfast at school.

lxc_b3b1c2b0f67a4604.text: Some children can get school breakfast for free.

lxc_d31e180a6ebc819e.text: After breakfast, children pack a bag.

lxc_d70eb1a9b300479f.text: A school bag is called a backpack.

lxc_782cc4fc688136c1.text: They put in books, pencils and a water bottle.

lxc_8616cbb2b7854f77.text: Some children put a lunch box in too.

lxc_90d233680563b99c.text: Some children walk with a parent.

lxc_35338259408f991b.text: Many children ride a yellow school bus.

lxc_364fc2cfd9c25ca2.text: The bus stops near their home.

lxc_12188d28c774287d.text: Children get on the bus and sit with friends.

lxc_b977aaec57022e60.text: Children get off and say hello to their teacher.

lxc_788e0cc25c502119.text: In about half of the states, children say the Pledge of Allegiance every day at school.

lxc_13714394411a9643.text: This is a short promise to the country.

lxc_2f37a316e426a2a0.text: Children stand and look at the flag.

lxc_1d12121d3aa5b0f3.text: The teacher reads a story out loud.

lxc_6b3c26ba86940698.text: Some children read in small groups.

lxc_826ecaf8fa715466.text: The teacher walks around and helps them.

lxc_97ae7b56e59cfe9d.text: Children count, add and take away.

lxc_63b627d0ccf841a8.text: They use numbers, blocks and pictures.

lxc_03e004c6744d1d8f.text: The teacher writes on the board.

lxc_8802e2ebeb4df414.text: Children raise their hand with questions.

lxc_7c2f5337347e1d60.text: In the middle of the day, children have a play break.

lxc_2dffd05ea30a9d45.text: In the USA, this break is called recess.

lxc_b157704410cebd1d.text: They run, jump and play games.

lxc_598008445b6c89be.text: Many schools have a big eating room.

lxc_63f503d625386b03.text: It has long tables and many chairs.

lxc_bb2b8adccef040be.text: Children sit and eat with friends.

lxc_5fdab980de863725.text: Some children bring lunch from home.

lxc_fa61f0c0227a6285.text: A lunch box can have a sandwich, an apple, carrots or crackers.

lxc_2d5d43d35cd0e593.text: School lunch can be pizza, chicken, rice, salad or fruit.

lxc_8b18c53802b142bc.text: Some children get school meals for free or at a lower price.

lxc_b28fb35e6fc40cef.text: The afternoon can have different subjects.

lxc_59b6245c3ecfaece.text: A subject is one part of learning, like math or art.

lxc_9313abbe95fb335c.text: They cut paper and make things.

lxc_3694106a0af35cda.text: Some children play small drums or bells.

lxc_2d8be208373e3efb.text: A gym is a big room for sports.

lxc_db0c52a36b0615da.text: They run, throw balls and play team games.

lxc_1c1284d6167f11cb.text: Children look at plants, water or small animals.

lxc_97e465dfadf594c9.text: At the end of the day, children tidy up.

lxc_f11cc33dc1f3d2c4.text: Some children put their chairs on the desks.

lxc_669c528826c916f4.text: Then they get their backpacks and coats.

lxc_9dbb85356846bd9f.text: The school day ends in the afternoon.

lxc_087ea185e7872646.text: Many children go home on the yellow bus.

lxc_e3791eec735fe42d.text: Some children walk home with an adult.

lxc_7fa33e28cbe8485b.text: Many children are hungry after school.

lxc_a207fea18bc386e4.text: They eat a snack at home.

lxc_eac24e79d98e8946.text: A snack is a small food between meals.

lxc_68b37b7a6908cb50.text: It can be an apple, cheese, crackers or a cookie.

lxc_9fe4c623d8e3b9e1.text: Homework is school work at home.

lxc_65068ae18c28b3d6.text: It can be a short book or a few math questions.

lxc_469a4350d57a3a7a.text: Some children play outside with friends.

lxc_aa7652ebf1b68f9c.text: They play ball in the yard or at the park.

lxc_6b9913871bc88520.text: A yard is the grass next to a house.

lxc_393a534a18a86ae8.text: Many children do activities after school.

lxc_97e06fddb5f377b7.text: Some children play sports, like soccer, basketball or baseball.

lxc_5f1ca71a0501c79f.text: Some children go to music or art class.

lxc_8e5068053563e404.text: Some children go to a club.

lxc_53ffa8ca4b8c0a74.text: A club is a group with the same hobby.

lxc_462482c32645b319.text: Some children go to an after-school program at their school.

lxc_8697dd92db3bf238.text: There, they get help with reading and math.

lxc_985d5d4558829ef9.text: Some children play with brothers, sisters or friends.

lxc_c9dee8ce14286b7d.text: In the evening, the family eats dinner.

lxc_cfefc147c74bae62.text: Dinner can be pasta, chicken, rice, tacos or soup with vegetables.

lxc_eec75a07be11b3ac.text: Some families eat together at the table.

lxc_43350a740d3d53c3.text: They put plates and forks on the table.

lxc_2b5679557e1e5ddf.text: After dinner, they take their plates to the sink.

lxc_613bae5e7542ac76.text: Some children feed the dog or the cat.

lxc_ad1f850a45f99f77.text: They play with toys, draw or watch TV.

lxc_9d46a323361f5980.text: They take a bath or a shower.

lxc_6d514ecaa1098216.text: Pajamas are soft clothes for sleeping.

lxc_978ac30f488f2977.text: Then they brush their teeth again.

lxc_4b859b9c55ef2943.text: Many parents read a story at bedtime.

lxc_a6b3344bf2be3aab.text: Most children have a regular bedtime.

lxc_d1812b8541cb4062.text: This means the same bedtime on most nights.

lxc_2c6980600b6e6d96.text: Young children often have a regular bedtime.

lxc_719c48e4074e8f38.text: Older children have one less often.

lxc_2fa79e40eb68ea36.text: On the weekend, there is no school.

lxc_0b43a8e080162ac3.text: Children can sleep a little longer.

lxc_22105e2e42601efc.text: They play, see family and go to sports games.

lxc_f4503c872096cfc7.text: You visit a school in the USA for one day.

lxc_b818390899b5f501.text: You walk into the big, loud cafeteria with your lunch box.

lxc_03ab57f4c9b4831f.text: A girl named Mia sits at a long table.

lxc_465f3bddff442208.text: There is a free chair next to her.

lxc_c048aaa7a8dbcfce.text: Your goal is to sit with Mia, talk about lunch and after school, and say goodbye at the end of lunch.

lxc_936fcd974bb3baae.text: Tell a partner about your day.

lxc_49a5a45c1e1888e4.text: Use short sentences, from morning to night.

lxc_89dfa324b9fe8b28.text: Say what time you wake up and what you eat for breakfast.

lxc_b2221860aa647dcb.text: Say how you go to school.

lxc_e5c5c3d0a7069128.text: Name your classes in the morning and the afternoon.

lxc_dd3a131c15f24817.text: Say what you eat for lunch and where you eat it.

lxc_b25a58c3ffa9bb03.text: Say what you do after school and before bed.

lxc_d27315e03608368a.text: Then ask your partner the same questions.

lxc_68b36f52cfdf9755.text: Find two things that are the same in your days.

lxc_92f9439d01c3a27a.text: Find one thing that is different from a day in the USA.
